title: School voucher program on student test scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Two-way fixed effects Difference-in-Differences (DID).
- Why: The voucher program begins in period 4 for treated districts only, with untreated districts serving as controls. We observe a balanced panel over time for districts before and after the policy, enabling DID with district and time fixed effects.
- Estimand: Average treatment effect on the treated (ATT), captured by the coefficient on treated × post.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of vouchers, treated and control districts would have had the same evolution in test scores.
  - No anticipation: Treated districts did not change behavior before the formal start (period 4).
  - Stable composition and no spillovers: District composition and testing are stable; no cross-district spillovers of vouchers.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 0) Setup ---------------------------------------------------------------------
req_pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest", "dplyr", "broom")
for (p in req_pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  }
}
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# 1) Read data -----------------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s03_data.csv"
df <- fread(path)

# Basic checks
n_units <- df[, uniqueN(unit_id)]
n_periods <- df[, uniqueN(period)]
cat("Loaded data. Districts:", n_units, "| Periods:", n_periods, "| Rows:", nrow(df), "\n")

# 2) Main DID: TWFE with unit and period FE, clustered SE at district ----------
# Outcome is mean-centered standardized test score (y)
did_main <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df, vcov = ~ unit_id)

main_est <- tidy(did_main) %>% filter(term == "treat_x_post")
ci_main <- confint(did_main, "treat_x_post")

cat("\nMain DID (TWFE, cluster by district):\n")
cat(sprintf("  ATT (treated x post) = %.4f\n", main_est$estimate))
cat(sprintf("  SE = %.4f | 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f] | p = %.4g\n",
            main_est$std.error, ci_main[1], ci_main[2], main_est$p.value))

# 3) Robustness A: Two-way clustered SE (district and period) ------------------
did_twoc <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df, vcov = ~ unit_id + period)
twoc_est <- tidy(did_twoc) %>% filter(term == "treat_x_post")
ci_twoc <- confint(did_twoc, "treat_x_post")

cat("\nRobustness A (Two-way clustering: district & period):\n")
cat(sprintf("  ATT = %.4f | SE = %.4f | 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f] | p = %.4g\n",
            twoc_est$estimate, twoc_est$std.error, ci_twoc[1], ci_twoc[2], twoc_est$p.value))

# 4) Robustness B: Add unit-specific linear trends -----------------------------
# Using fixest 'slopes' to allow a unit-specific slope in time (period)
did_trend <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, slopes = ~ period, data = df, vcov = ~ unit_id)
trend_est <- tidy(did_trend) %>% filter(term == "treat_x_post")
ci_trend <- confint(did_trend, "treat_x_post")

cat("\nRobustness B (Unit-specific linear trends):\n")
cat(sprintf("  ATT = %.4f | SE = %.4f | 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f] | p = %.4g\n",
            trend_est$estimate, trend_est$std.error, ci_trend[1], ci_trend[2], trend_est$p.value))

# 5) Event-study for pre-trends and dynamics -----------------------------------
# Relative time where 0 = first treated period (period 4)
df <- df %>% mutate(rel_t = period - 4L)

# Event-study: interactions Treated x RelativeTime with FE and clustering
es_mod <- feols(y ~ i(rel_t, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period, data = df, vcov = ~ unit_id)

es_tidy <- tidy(es_mod) %>%
  filter(grepl("^i\\(rel_t,treated\\)::", term)) %>%
  mutate(k = as.integer(sub(".*::(-?\\d+)$", "\\1", term))) %>%
  arrange(k)

# Print key pre-period (leads) and post-period (lags)
pre_leads <- es_tidy %>% filter(k <= -2)
post_effects <- es_tidy %>% filter(k >= 0)

cat("\nEvent-study (coefficients are Treated x 1[RelTime = k], base = k = -1 (period 3)):\n")
if (nrow(pre_leads) > 0) {
  cat("  Pre-policy leads (k <= -2):\n")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(pre_leads))) {
    cat(sprintf("    k = %2d: coef = %.4f | SE = %.4f | p = %.4g\n",
                pre_leads$k[i], pre_leads$estimate[i], pre_leads$std.error[i], pre_leads$p.value[i]))
  }
} else {
  cat("  No pre-policy leads available.\n")
}
if (nrow(post_effects) > 0) {
  cat("  Post-policy dynamics (k >= 0):\n")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(post_effects))) {
    cat(sprintf("    k = %2d: coef = %.4f | SE = %.4f | p = %.4g\n",
                post_effects$k[i], post_effects$estimate[i], post_effects$std.error[i], post_effects$p.value[i]))
  }
}

# 6) Placebo test: pre-periods only, fake policy at period >= 2 ----------------
pre_df <- df %>% filter(period <= 3) %>%
  mutate(placebo_post = as.integer(period >= 2),
         treat_x_placebo = treated * placebo_post)

did_placebo <- feols(y ~ treat_x_placebo | unit_id + period, data = pre_df, vcov = ~ unit_id)
pl_est <- tidy(did_placebo) %>% filter(term == "treat_x_placebo")
ci_pl <- confint(did_placebo, "treat_x_placebo")

cat("\nPlacebo DID (pre-periods only, fake start at period 2):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Placebo ATT = %.4f | SE = %.4f | 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f] | p = %.4g\n",
            pl_est$estimate, pl_est$std.error, ci_pl[1], ci_pl[2], pl_est$p.value))

# 7) Final printed result ------------------------------------------------------
cat("\nFinal reported estimate (Main DID, cluster by district):\n")
cat(sprintf("  ATT (treated x post) = %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n",
            main_est$estimate, main_est$std.error))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive, if vouchers expand school choice and competition, improving outcomes.
- Magnitude: Modest. I expect an ATT around 0.05–0.15 in mean-centered standardized test-score units (roughly a few hundredths to a tenth of a standard deviation), with effects that emerge from period 4 onward and no significant pre-trends in periods 1–3. Robustness checks (two-way clustering, unit trends, placebo) should not overturn the sign or significance if the program truly improved scores.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=voucher districts, control=non-voucher; shock=program introduction
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Test scores increase significantly in voucher districts after program launch
